# Correctness review: PR #257

Head: d968afe002b745c8f43eac5a6d80783bf8b88601
Base: 70d01ba27a6258efa69b66d30ba5671ee1d30b68
Verdict: BLOCK

## R257-001: the canonical test recipe deterministically fails on macOS

`justfile:118` now starts the complete Vitest suite under `/usr/bin/nice -n 19`. The existing test at `harness/scripts/shared-build.test.ts:272-311` launches `shared-build.sh`, which applies another relative nice increment of 19. On macOS that child reports niceness 20, while lines 306-309 require exactly 19 for all three commands. Thus ordinary `just test`, and the test stage of `harness checks`, fail on the supported fleet host even though the scheduling change itself is conservative.

Read-only OS receipt, not a test-suite run:

```
/usr/bin/nice -n 19 /usr/bin/nice -n 19 /bin/sh -c '/bin/ps -o ni= -p "$$"'
20
```

The fake cargo reads the same process property with `ps -o nice= -p $$`. Existing independent evidence in `docs/retros/pij-previous-firefly-plan-227.md:3-6` records exactly this assertion failure under an outer nice wrapper. Performance reviewer pij-public-cobra independently raised the same issue.

Fix the test's scheduling contract to account for inherited niceness and platform saturation without removing the new niced recipe or weakening the check that shared-build actually applies its wrapper. CI does not disprove this failure: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs bare `npm test` on Linux, not `just test` on macOS. This is a normal-use harness correctness bug, not an optional mutation or hardening request under C34.

## Nonblocking follow-up: explain the local smoke skip

`harness/scripts/smoke.test.ts:33-43` says the reason is recorded, but the missing-artifact branch only selects `describe.skip("runWatchdogSmoke", ...)`. It emits neither the missing artifact path nor a repair command. Add an explicit skip diagnostic or reason-bearing suite title. CI is correctly strict: it builds pij-rs before npm test and sets `PIJ_RS_BIN_REQUIRED=1`; the exact-head CI log confirms the watchdog smoke ran. This note does not add a gate.

## Reviewed behavior

- The target resolver uses the absolute git common directory's parent. In a normal clone that is its main checkout; linked worktrees and this detached review worktree share that clone's target. A different ordinary clone has its own common directory and does not accidentally use this clone's target. Read-only execution here selected the canonical checkout's target; relative and absolute overrides containing spaces were preserved. No directories were created.
- Debug/test building recipes retain their package selections and arguments and use the existing shared-build lock, source refresh, disk floor and nice wrapper. rust-check keeps clippy and tests under one lock hold. Release deployment recipes retain their release profile, install source and stamping, with only the nice wrapper added; their documented shared-build exemption is unchanged.
- The fixture no longer contains a cargo build path and copies an existing binary before executing it. The PATH shim refuses the listed build-class commands and delegates nonbuilding commands to the next inherited PATH cargo. Its executable path is quoted, and it skips its own physical directory. This is a same-user development guard under C33, not a new hostile-PATH security boundary. No new eval or machine-specific path was added.
- The recipe-cost sensor is a direct-command syntax check, not a shell parser. Manual provider/timing probes are not exempted by recipe-name allowlist: their script invocations do not match its runner patterns. That matches the declared scope.
- Target selection and the no-build rule are policies, not deletion brakes. Nothing deletes existing targets.

## Evidence and cost

No local builds, test suites, dependency installation or code edits were performed.

`just pr-freeze 257` passed twice, most recently immediately before preparing this verdict: exact head agreement, main base, CLEAN, all five checks successful, nondraft, migration and Delivers checks satisfied. `git diff --check 70d01ba2...HEAD` passed. The review worktree remained clean and had no target directory.

CI run 44464878980 is successful at the exact reviewed head. Node 24 job 135360150049 shows smoke.test.ts 9 tests passed, shared-build.test.ts 19 passed, recipe-cost.test.ts 8 passed, cargo-tripwire.test.ts 4 passed, and 105 test files passed / 1 skipped. Rust lint and test jobs also passed. These are CI receipts, not claims of local execution.

The PR's before/after build receipts report a missing-binary fixture build of 2.4 GB and 69 seconds before, versus zero nested builds after; shared debug artifacts around 15 GB; route inventory 49 seconds; smoke 79 seconds total. Those build/disk measurements were not repeated, per the no-build/no-test review contract. Source inspection confirms removal of the nested build path. New contention is intentional: the heavy recipes now wait for the same lock rather than building concurrently. Each waiting caller retains the existing 20-second poll, with one df, mkdir and sleep per poll, approximately 0.15 launches/second/caller. There is no new daemon loop or per-seat recurring launch; the cargo tripwire is per attempted cargo invocation, not periodic.

Live baseline, 2026-11-19 05:31:01-05:31:22 UTC: `/usr/bin/nice -n 19 just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json` measured 87.4 machine launches/second over 20 seconds. Daemon spawn counters stayed 1531 -> 1531, with no per-operation change. Daemon PID 36530 had ps CPU 20.0%, RSS 151616 KiB, nice 0. Load averages moved from 20.95/24.95/40.75 at 05:30 to 16.00/22.55/38.59 at 05:31. This is a current shared-host baseline, not a controlled before/after performance comparison.

## Harness feedback

magicWand: CI should exercise the canonical niced test entry point, with platform-aware evidence for macOS scheduling, rather than proving only the bare npm path.

difficulties: Linux CI passes a scheduling assertion that contradicts the new normal macOS recipe; the preexisting retro already contained the diagnostic. Encode that lesson in the scheduling test instead of asking every coder to explain away a red gate.
